info.description:
Internal API of the Boogle Engine Indexing Service. Provider: Indexing Service.
Intended consumer: the Control Module, which orchestrates ingestion, indexing and publication.
It is not part of the front-end contract.
info.title: Boogle Engine Indexing API

post.description:
- **Provider:** Indexing Service
- **Intended consumer:** Control Module (internal, administrative): after the service restarts, or to re-index
every book after the tokenizer or the metadata parser changes

Builds a brand-new metadata catalog and inverted index from every complete book in the datalake, written to
fresh datamart collections. Books still being ingested are not included. The request has no body.

**Completion and publication.** Synchronous and atomic. The new index is built aside while the previous one keeps
answering, and replaces it in a single step once every book is indexed: a 200 response means the new index is
published. If the rebuild fails or is interrupted, it is discarded and the previous index stays published
unchanged; a half-built index is never visible.

**Idempotency and consistency.** Repeating it over the same datalake produces the same index. Only one rebuild runs
at a time: another request meanwhile gets `409 rebuild_in_progress`. POST /index/update calls during a rebuild are
not blocked: they are recorded and replayed on the rebuilt index after the swap, so the published result never loses them.

**Timeouts and retries expected of the caller.** The duration grows with the datalake (the assignment's reference
is about 35 s per 1000 books) and is capped by the service's rebuild budget (`-rebuild-timeout`, 10 minutes by
default). Keep the connection open with a client timeout above that budget: disconnecting abandons the rebuild.
- `409 rebuild_in_progress`: do not start another one; wait and poll GET /index/status until `last_update` changes.
- `503 rebuild_interrupted` and `500 internal_error`: the previous index is still published; retry later with backoff.
post.summary: Rebuild the whole index from the datalake

500.description: internal_error: the datalake could not be listed or a book could not be indexed

503.description: rebuild_interrupted: the rebuild budget ran out or the caller disconnected

get.description:
- **Provider:** Indexing Service
- **Intended consumer:** Control Module (internal, operational): to follow indexing progress, detect the end of a
rebuild and record memory use during benchmarks

**Fields.** `books_indexed` counts the published books of the metadata datamart. `last_update` is the UTC time of the
last successful update or rebuild (at startup, the time the adapter was created). `index_size_MB` is a rough
estimate of the stored index data: the document bytes of the MongoDB datamart.

**Consistency.** Describes the published index only; a running rebuild shows up when it is published.

**Idempotency, timeouts and retries.** Read-only, cheap and safe to poll at any time; a client timeout of about
5 s is enough. Retry on timeouts and connection errors.

post.description:
- **Provider:** Indexing Service
- **Intended consumer:** Control Module (internal API, not exposed to the front-end)
- **Position in the workflow:** second step of a book's lifecycle. Call it once POST /ingest/{book_id} has returned
200 (or GET /ingest/status/{book_id} answers `available`); the datalake only exposes completely written books.

Reads the book from the datalake, extracts its metadata (title, author, language, publication and release years)
and adds its body terms to the inverted index. The request has no body.

**Completion and publication.** Synchronous: a 200 response means the work has fully completed and the book's
metadata record and postings are in the published index, visible to every request that starts afterwards. If a
rebuild is running, the book is recorded and replayed on the rebuilt index right after it is published, so the
rebuild cannot lose it.

**Idempotency and consistency.** Safe to repeat: re-indexing a book that is already indexed replaces its metadata
record and adds no duplicate postings, so the index ends up exactly as after the first call. Updates of different
books run in parallel; concurrent updates of the same book are harmless.

**Timeouts and retries expected of the caller.** One update reads one book from local disk and usually takes
milliseconds (about a second for the largest books); a client timeout of 30 s is ample and an update is never
blocked by a running rebuild.
- Client timeout, connection error or `500 internal_error`: retry the same request with exponential backoff.
- `404 book_not_found`: the book is not completely ingested. Ingest it first, then retry; repeating alone will not help.
- The index is stored in the MongoDB datamart, so indexed books stay searchable across service restarts.

200.description: The book is in the published index

400.description: invalid_book_id: book_id is not a positive integer

404.description: book_not_found: the datalake holds no complete copy of the book

500.description: internal_error: the book could not be read or indexed

message.example: query parameter "limit" must be an integer between 1 and 100

books_indexed.description: Books in the published metadata catalog

index_size_MB.description: Rough estimate in MiB: size of the stored index data (datamart document bytes)

last_update.description: UTC time of the last successful update or rebuild; at startup, when the empty index was published

books_processed.description: Books of the datalake that the published index was rebuilt from

elapsed_time.description: Duration of the rebuild in Go duration syntax (time.ParseDuration), rounded to milliseconds
